subject: FedRAMP readiness: federal scope checklist and ISO sync questions
messages:
From: Sara Morales <sara@adeptcompliance.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FedRAMP intake — narrow scope checklist and ISO overlap questions

Hi Sean,

Thanks for agreeing to kick off the FedRAMP readiness intake. To get the initial assessment scoped correctly we need a couple of clarifications from your side before our call:

1) Target authorization level (Low / Moderate / High) and whether you expect a P-ATO or agency-led ATO.
2) Confirmation of the in-scope product boundary (hosted API only, dedicated clusters, private deployments?).
3) A short list of control owners (who we should ask for evidence) and an initial sample window (e.g., last 6 months).
4) Any existing ISO 27001 artifacts you intend to reuse for FedRAMP (statement of applicability, risk register, control mappings).

I attached a proposed kickoff agenda and a brief checklist — please return with the requested items or let me know if the agency wants to expand the scope.

Attachments: redwood-inference-fedramp-kickoff-agenda.pdf (PDF)

Best,
Sara Morales
Manager, Assessments
Adept Compliance LLC
--
Adept Compliance | adeptcompliance.com
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Sara Morales <sara@adeptcompliance.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FedRAMP intake — narrow scope checklist and ISO overlap questions

Sara — thanks, and appreciate the clear checklist. Answers inline below; attaching an early control mapping draft we started for ISO.

1) Target level: Moderate. The agency is pursuing a full agency ATO rather than a P-ATO (we heard this from procurement).
2) Scope: primary hosted API (public-hosted endpoints) + Dedicated for customers with reserved capacity. Private on-prem deployments are out of scope for the federal authorization; they will be documented separately.
3) Control owners (initial):
   - Security logging & retention: Karthik Iyer (Infra)
   - Identity & access mgmt: Mina Haddad (Security Ops)
   - Change control / CI: Laura Bennett (Platform Eng)
   - Legal / contracts: myself (sean_gallagher) – for any data flow / customer agreement questions
4) ISO artifacts: we have an SoA and an in-progress control mapping (attached). We plan to reuse parts of the ISO evidence where appropriate but expect gaps for some FedRAMP-specific controls (system categorization and continuous monitoring evidence).

Attachments: iso-control-mapping-draft.xlsx (XLSX)

Action items: can you confirm the sample window you prefer (3 vs 6 months) and whether the agency will require AWS-specific diagrams (we run multi-cloud but most production workloads are AWS)?

Thanks — I’ll loop in the control owners to provide any technical artifacts.

—Sean Gallagher
Director, Strategic Accounts (acting on program intake)
Redwood Inference
From: Sara Morales <sara@adeptcompliance.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: fedinfosec@govagency.gov, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 04 Apr 2027 12:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FedRAMP intake — narrow scope checklist and ISO overlap questions

Thanks, Sean — that helps a lot. Agency confirmed Moderate is the right baseline. For planning:

- Preferred sample window: 6 months for initial assessment (they want a reasonable activity history).
- AWS diagrams: Yes, the agency would like cloud architecture diagrams showing VPC/subnet boundaries, encryption-in-transit points, and where customer data resides. If multi-cloud, call out non-AWS services but provide deeper AWS artifacts.
- Evidence expectation: system security plan (SSP) template will be shared by us; we expect control-owner artifacts (screenshots, runbooks, policy documents) and at least one week of logging evidence for logging-related controls.

I’ll put the SSP link in the kickoff agenda and propose time for a 60-min intake on Tue 2027-04-12.

Sara

Attachments referenced: none in this message

Sara / team,

Quick control-owner confirmations and notes:
- Logging & retention: Karthik — we currently retain auth and API access logs for 90 days in ELK; longer retention is archived to S3 (cold) for up to 12 months.
- IAM: I own roles/policy reviews; we have SSO (OIDC) with SCIM provisioning and MFA for all staff.
- Config/change control: Laura — CI pipelines are audited and we have one approved deployment window per day.

Gaps to flag up front:
- Continuous monitoring automation for FedRAMP (agent deployment and centralized alerting) is partial — we have dashboards but not fully automated evidence extraction.
- We need to produce an SSP that aligns with the agency template (Sara: please share the template ASAP).

I’ll gather the screenshots/runbooks requested and coordinate with Karthik to produce an initial logging extract for the 6-month window.

—Mina
Security Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

Folks — technical clarifications from infra:
- Logging: we can produce ELK exports for the last 6 months, and an S3 archive manifest showing archived log buckets. Samples will include API request traces, auth events, and admin console access.
- Key management: we use customer-managed KMS keys for Dedicated clusters; hosted API uses RW-managed keys. If the agency requires KMS evidence, we can provide KMS rotation logs and IAM policies.
- KV cache / ephemeral state: we do not persist unencrypted customer inputs in caches beyond token-level transient storage; will prepare a short runbook describing lifecycle.

Attachments we will provide in the intake packet:
- logging-sample-README.txt (text stub describing files)
- kms-rotation-extract.csv (CSV)

I’ll coordinate with Mina on the runbooks and with Laura on CI audit reports.

—Karthik

1) Scope confirmed: Hosted API + Dedicated pools (Private on-prem out of scope).
2) Authorization level: Moderate, agency-led ATO.
3) Sample window: 6 months; Karthik will deliver logging extracts and S3 manifest.
4) Control owners assigned: Mina (IAM), Karthik (Logging/KMS), Laura (Change/CI), Sean (Contracts).
5) Evidence artifacts to deliver by 2027-04-14: SSP draft (using agency template), logging extracts, runbooks for KV cache lifecycle, CI audit report, KMS rotation extract.
6) Intake meeting scheduled: Tue 2027-04-12 10:00 PT — Sara / FedAgency team to send calendar invite with the SSP link.

Please flag any blocker by EOD Mon 2027-04-11. I’ll assemble the packet and upload to the DocuSign/drive link once artifacts are ready.
